rationale: Theorems 1-2 hold for a Feller-process proxy of SGD; the bound is never evaluated numerically, and CIFAR experiments only correlate the BG index with the generalisation gap.
Theorem 5/Corollary 1 are analytical bounds on an LTI model with unknown G* and J*; the simulations report controller cost, not the bound.

Theorem 1 proves a statistical claim about learned classifiers (adversarial error >= c1 w.p. 1-delta over m samples), and Theorem 3(i) gives a positive robustness guarantee; the object (D, l_p balls) is identifiable.
Learning-theoretic sample-complexity bound on population adversarial risk, not PAC-Bayes; matches classes.csv GEN.
Evaluated only on synthetic data, MNIST and CIFAR-10/100; no vehicle task.
Codebook: image classifiers count as perception; experiments use MNIST/CIFAR classifiers.
R_Adv,2rho(f;D) is a probability over the data distribution D: a distribution of inputs.
The bound holds with probability 1-delta over the i.i.d. sample S_m (data distribution), not over certifier randomness.
The adversarial error is defined over l_p balls B_gamma(x) (mostly l_inf).
The sample-size condition m >= |zeta|/(eta c2) log(|zeta|/delta) is a concentration/union-bound argument from samples.
Eq.(3) mass conditions and i.i.d. label-flip noise are stated, but no evidence is given that the benchmarks satisfy them.
The headline bound is proven for abstract distributions; PGD experiments are qualitative and never instantiate the bound.
Theorem 2 bounds each state's policy distance to the Nash set; not a bounded-horizon reach set or a distribution. Rule 6: choose the smaller scope.
Theorem 2 bounds (1/|S|) sum_s dist^2 and Theorem 1 bounds an average duality gap; codebook E covers a bound on an average.
Theorem 3/Corollary 5 use sample-based estimators to carry the guarantee to the learning setting w.p. 1-delta under Assumption 1.
The headline bound values (Corollary 6) are certificates computed on the actual sampled networks, not measured test risks.
